sentences.en: There is a statue in South Carolina honoring a man who is known as the father of modern gynecology.
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州有一座雕像，旨在纪念一位被称为“现代妇科之父”的人。

sentences.en: The inscription on the statue reads,
sentences.zh: 雕像上的铭文写道：

sentences.en: The first surgeon of the ages in ministry to women, treating alike, empress, and slave.
sentences.zh: “历代以来服务女性的第一外科医生，对皇后与奴隶一视同仁。”

sentences.en: J.
sentences.zh: 而且事情

sentences.en: Marion Sims was a physician who was born in South Carolina in 1813.
sentences.zh: 马里恩·西姆斯（J. Marion Sims）是一位医生，1813年出生于南卡罗来纳州。

sentences.en: This is Vanessa Northington Gamble.
sentences.zh: 这位是凡妮莎·诺辛顿·甘布尔（Vanessa Northington Gamble）。

sentences.en: She's a physician and medical historian at the George Washington University,
sentences.zh: 她是乔治华盛顿大学的医生兼医学历史学家，

sentences.en: we asked her to come in to tell us the story of J.
sentences.zh: 我们邀请她来讲述J.

sentences.en: Marion Sims,
sentences.zh: 马里恩·西姆斯的故事，

sentences.en: who was memorialized in statues not only in South Carolina,
sentences.zh: 他不仅在南卡罗来纳州，

sentences.en: but also in Montgomery, Alabama, and Central Park in New York City.
sentences.zh: 还在阿拉巴马州蒙哥马利市和纽约市中央公园都有雕像纪念。

sentences.en: He started a clinic in Montgomery, Alabama.
sentences.zh: 他在阿拉巴马州的蒙哥马利开了一家诊所。

sentences.en: And at the time, in order to survive financially,
sentences.zh: 当时，为了维持生计，

sentences.en: he also was a plantation physician, where he took care of the enslaved on plantations.
sentences.zh: 他还担任种植园医生，负责照看种植园里的奴隶。

sentences.en: This is where the story of Sims becomes complicated.
sentences.zh: 西姆斯的故事也正是在这里变得复杂起来。

sentences.en: Because yes, the inscription on a statue in South Carolina is true.
sentences.zh: 因为没错，南卡罗来纳州雕像上的铭文确实是真的。

sentences.en: He did invent techniques that help women to this day.
sentences.zh: 他确实发明了至今仍在帮助女性的技术。

sentences.en: He treated slaves as well as high society.
sentences.zh: 他既治疗奴隶，也治疗上流社会人士。

sentences.en: He once treated Empress Eugenie, the last Empress of France.
sentences.zh: 他曾为法国末代皇后欧仁妮皇后治病。

sentences.en: But there is something not mentioned on the inscriptions on the statues.
sentences.zh: 但雕像铭文上并没有提到一些事情。

sentences.en: Starting in 1845, he started to conduct experiments on enslaved women.
sentences.zh: 从1845年开始，他开始对被奴役的女性进行实验。

sentences.en: And why we talk about Sims today and why that statue was there
sentences.zh: 我们今天之所以谈论西姆斯，以及那座雕像之所以存在，

sentences.en: is that he perfected a technique to repair a condition called vesicovaginal fistula.
sentences.zh: 是因为他完善了一种修复膀胱阴道瘘的技术。

sentences.en: And let me tell you what that means.
sentences.zh: 让我来告诉你这意味着什么。

sentences.en: It basically means that there is an opening between the vagina and also the bladder,
sentences.zh: 它基本上是指阴道与膀胱之间，

sentences.en: or the vagina and the rectum, which usually comes after traumatic childbirth.
sentences.zh: 或者阴道与直肠之间出现了一个开口，这通常发生在创伤性分娩之后。

sentences.en: And Sims started in 1845, 1846, according to some sources,
sentences.zh: 据一些资料记载，西姆斯在1845年、1846年开始了

sentences.en: a series of experiments to repair these fistulas.
sentences.zh: 一系列修复这些瘘管的实验。

sentences.en: This condition was highly stigmatized and dangerous for these women.
sentences.zh: 这种疾病对这些女性来说不仅危险，而且极具羞辱性。

sentences.en: There was no treatment.
sentences.zh: 当时根本没有治疗方法。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, you could say Sims was doing what doctors are supposed to do
sentences.zh: 所以一方面，你可以说西姆斯是在履行医生的职责，

sentences.en: by taking these women on as patients.
sentences.zh: 接收这些女性作为病人。

sentences.en: But there's another side to what Sims did.
sentences.zh: 但西姆斯的所作所为还有另一面。

sentences.en: He wanted to be a trailblazing researcher.
sentences.zh: 他渴望成为一名开创性的研究者。

sentences.en: And these women, their bodies, became props in his journey of scientific discovery.
sentences.zh: 而这些女性，她们的身体，成了他科学发现之旅中的道具。

sentences.en: These women were property.
sentences.zh: 这些女性是财产。

sentences.en: These women could not consent.
sentences.zh: 这些女性无法表示同意。

sentences.en: These women also had value to the slaveholders for production and reproduction.
sentences.zh: 对于奴隶主来说，这些女性在生产和繁衍方面也具有价值。

sentences.en: How much work they could do in the fields.
sentences.zh: 她们能在田间做多少活，

sentences.en: How many enslaved children they could produce.
sentences.zh: 她们能生下多少奴隶后代。

sentences.en: And by having these fistulas, they could not continue with childbirth.
sentences.zh: 而患有这些瘘管病，她们就无法继续生育。

sentences.en: And also have difficulty working.
sentences.zh: 而且工作起来也很困难。

sentences.en: There are ten slave women central to the story.
sentences.zh: 在这个故事中，有十名奴隶女性处于核心地位。

sentences.en: Three are named by Sims in his writing.
sentences.zh: 西姆斯在著作中提到了其中三人的名字。

sentences.en: These women were brought to him by their owners.
sentences.zh: 这些女性是被她们的主人带到他那里的。

sentences.en: The first woman was named Anarka.
sentences.zh: 第一位女性名叫安娜卡（Anarka）。

sentences.en: Anarka was a 17-year-old enslaved woman
sentences.zh: 安娜卡是一名17岁的被奴役女性，

sentences.en: who had just undergone a very traumatic delivery.
sentences.zh: 她刚刚经历了一次非常痛苦的分娩。

sentences.en: Some sources say that she was in labor for three days.
sentences.zh: 一些资料说她分娩过程长达三天。

sentences.en: At first, he did not want to treat her.
sentences.zh: 起初，他并不想治疗她。

sentences.en: He was not interested in treating women.
sentences.zh: 他对治疗女性并不感兴趣。

sentences.en: But then what he started to do from a period from 1845 to 1849,
sentences.zh: 但随后，在1845年到1849年期间，他开始做的事情是，

sentences.en: he did a series of experimental surgeries on these women.
sentences.zh: 他对这些女性进行了一系列实验性手术。

sentences.en: And he uses sutures to try to close up this opening.
sentences.zh: 他使用缝合线试图缝合这个开口。

sentences.en: Now, presumably this would have been painful.
sentences.zh: 可以想见，这一定很痛苦。

sentences.en: It was very painful.
sentences.zh: 确实非常痛苦。

sentences.en: And he talks about how Lucy, one of the three women,
sentences.zh: 他提到露西（Lucy），也就是那三名女性之一，

sentences.en: almost felt as if she were going to die.
sentences.zh: 感觉自己快要死了。

sentences.en: That she cried out in pain so much because of these surgeries.
sentences.zh: 因为这些手术，她痛得大声尖叫。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he writes that the women wanted the surgery
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他写道，这些女性想要接受手术，

sentences.en: because they did not want to have the condition anymore.
sentences.zh: 因为她们不想再忍受这种疾病了。

sentences.en: Were the surgeries that he was performing on them performed without anesthesia?
sentences.zh: 他给她们做的手术是在没有麻醉的情况下进行的吗？

sentences.en: They were performed without anesthesia.
sentences.zh: 确实是在没有麻醉的情况下进行的。

sentences.en: There was a belief at the time
sentences.zh: 当时有一种观念认为，

sentences.en: that black people did not feel pain in the same way.
sentences.zh: 黑人感受不到同样的疼痛。

sentences.en: They were not vulnerable to pain, especially black women.
sentences.zh: 她们对疼痛不敏感，尤其是黑人女性。

sentences.en: So that they had suffered pain in other parts of their lives.
sentences.zh: 认为她们在生活的其他方面已经受过苦了。

sentences.en: And their pain was ignored.
sentences.zh: 所以她们的痛苦被忽视了。

sentences.en: As Sims' reputation as a researcher grew,
sentences.zh: 随着西姆斯作为研究者的名声越来越大，

sentences.en: he began to invite other physicians to come watch as he performed the surgeries.
sentences.zh: 他开始邀请其他医生来观看他做手术。

sentences.en: So this surgery was done where black women were naked.
sentences.zh: 所以这项手术是在黑人女性赤身裸体的情况下进行的。

sentences.en: So when we think about it, I think we think about pain.
sentences.zh: 所以当我们思考这个问题时，我想我们首先想到的是疼痛。

sentences.en: We also need to think about how these women's dignity were also taken away from them.
sentences.zh: 我们还需要思考这些女性的尊严是如何被剥夺的。

sentences.en: For a long time, the surgeries didn't work.
sentences.zh: 很长一段时间里，手术都没有成功。

sentences.en: No, he's not successful at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 不，他一开始并不成功。

sentences.en: And so that's why these surgeries went on from 1846 to 1849.
sentences.zh: 所以这些手术从1846年一直持续到了1849年。

sentences.en: And finally, after 30 surgeries on one woman,
sentences.zh: 最终，在对同一名女性进行了30次手术后，

sentences.en: he was finally able to perfect his technique.
sentences.zh: 他终于完善了他的技术。

sentences.en: That woman was Annika.
sentences.zh: 那名女性就是安娜卡。

sentences.en: The two others who are named in Sims' papers are Betsy and Lucy.
sentences.zh: 西姆斯论文中提到的另外两人是贝齐（Betsy）和露西（Lucy）。

sentences.en: I asked Vanessa Gamble whether there was any way to know
sentences.zh: 我问凡妮莎·甘布尔，有没有办法知道

sentences.en: if these women actually wanted the surgeries.
sentences.zh: 这些女性是否真的想要接受手术。

sentences.en: We do not know that.
sentences.zh: 我们不得而知。

sentences.en: The only thing we know is that Sims said that these women,
sentences.zh: 我们唯一知道的是西姆斯说这些女性，

sentences.en: one of the women, clamorously wanted to have the surgery.
sentences.zh: 其中一名女性，强烈要求接受手术。

sentences.en: They wanted to be cured.
sentences.zh: 她们想要被治愈。

sentences.en: One of the things in the story that's missing
sentences.zh: 这个故事中缺失的一点，

sentences.en: are the words and voices of the women themselves,
sentences.zh: 是这些女性自己的话语和声音，

sentences.en: not being translated by SiMs.
sentences.zh: 而不是经过西姆斯转述的。

sentences.en: Sims, of course, has a self-interested reason
sentences.zh: 当然，西姆斯有自私的理由

sentences.en: to say that the women wanted what he was trying to do to them.
sentences.zh: 去宣称这些女性想要他强加给她们的东西。

sentences.en: Of course he has an intereSt.
sentences.zh: 他当然有私心。

sentences.en: And one of the interests is that it mutes the story of slavery in his work.
sentences.zh: 其中一个私心就是，这掩盖了他工作背后的奴隶制背景。

sentences.en: That it mutes the story that the foundations of modern gynecology
sentences.zh: 掩盖了现代妇科的基础

sentences.en: are based on the body and the pain of enslaved black women.
sentences.zh: 是建立在被奴役黑人女性的身体和痛苦之上的事实。

sentences.en: The statue in South Carolina that says that Sims treated
sentences.zh: 南卡罗来纳州的那座雕像说西姆斯对

sentences.en: empress and slave women alike.
sentences.zh: 皇后和奴隶女性一视同仁。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Is that true?
sentences.zh: 那是真的吗？

sentences.en: Was he treating white women the same way?
sentences.zh: 他对待白人女性也是一样的方式吗？

sentences.en: He did treat white women,
sentences.zh: 他确实治疗过白人女性，

sentences.en: but he treated white women with anesthesia.
sentences.zh: 但他给白人女性使用了麻醉。

sentences.en: Sims left in the 1850s.
sentences.zh: 西姆斯在19世纪50年代离开了。

sentences.en: He left Alabama and moved to New York City for health reasons.
sentences.zh: 他离开阿拉巴马州搬到了纽约市，是因为健康原因。

sentences.en: And he started a woman's hospital in 1855 there.
sentences.zh: 并于1855年在那里创办了一家妇女医院。

sentences.en: He gained a reputation as an excellent surgeon.
sentences.zh: 他获得了优秀外科医生的声誉。

sentences.en: And so that he did treat white women.
sentences.zh: 所以他确实治疗过白人女性。

sentences.en: But the technique had been perfected on the bodies of black women.
sentences.zh: 但这项技术是在黑人女性的身体上完善的。

sentences.en: When you hear about a story that took place 150 years ago,
sentences.zh: 当你听到一个发生在150年前的故事时，

sentences.en: there is a part of us that says,
sentences.zh: 我们内心的一部分会说，

sentences.en: that was pretty awful, but that was then, and this is now.
sentences.zh: 那太可怕了，但那是过去，现在不同了。

sentences.en: But a lot of your work has actually tried to broaden that idea and said,
sentences.zh: 但你的许多工作实际上试图拓宽这一观点，并指出，

sentences.en: yes, that was then, but some of what was then is also with us now.
sentences.zh: 是的，那是过去，但过去的一些东西现在依然存在。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, one of the things that...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，其中一件事……

sentences.en: I teach a course on the history of race and racism in American medicine.
sentences.zh: 我教授一门关于美国医学中种族和种族主义历史的课程。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I try to get across to my students
sentences.zh: 我试图向学生传达的一点是，

sentences.en: is that racism is a very flexible, very adaptive concept.
sentences.zh: 种族主义是一个非常灵活、非常适应性强的概念。

sentences.en: That, yes, black people are not thrown out of hospitals these days
sentences.zh: 是的，如今黑人不会因为是黑人而被赶出医院，

sentences.en: because they are black or not excluded from hospitals because they are black.
sentences.zh: 也不会因为是黑人而被拒之门外。

sentences.en: But our focus today is on what happens once one gets into the hospital.
sentences.zh: 但我们今天的重点是，一旦进入医院会发生什么。

sentences.en: It's striking as you say this because I feel like I've read studies in the last few years
sentences.zh: 你说这话时很引人深思，因为我觉得过去几年我读过一些研究，

sentences.en: looking at disparities in how people of color get treated for pain
sentences.zh: 关注20世纪末和21世纪初有色人种在疼痛治疗方面存在的差异。

sentences.en: in the late 20th century and the early 21st century.
sentences.zh: 感觉150年前发生的事情与今天发生的事情之间存在着某种联系。

sentences.en: It feels like there is a thread between what happened 150 years ago
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: and what's happening today.
sentences.zh: 我同意你的观点，因为我认为故事的一部分与医学界如何概念化黑人身体有关。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 约翰霍普金斯大学发布过一段关于镰状细胞病患者的视频。

sentences.en: I agree with you because I think part of the story has to deal with how black bodies are conceptualized
sentences.zh: 在视频中，这位女性说，

sentences.en: by the medical profession.
sentences.zh: 当我去看病时，即使我很痛苦，我也会确保自己穿戴整齐。

sentences.en: There is a video that Johns Hopkins put out about people with sickle cell disease.
sentences.zh: 因为如果我穿戴整齐，也许我会得到更好的治疗，

sentences.en: And in this video, this woman says,
sentences.zh: 而不会被视为寻求药物的人。

sentences.en: when I go to the hospital, even though I'm in pain, I make sure I get dressed up.
sentences.zh: 所以，在医学界如何看待黑人和黑人身体方面，这种偏见依然存在。

sentences.en: Because if I get dressed up, maybe I will be treated better
sentences.zh: 不过，马里恩·西姆斯发现的一些东西确实仍在被使用，或影响着今天的医疗实践，这也是事实。

sentences.en: and not be seen as somebody who is seeking drugs.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it still is there in terms of how the medical profession views black people and black bodies.
sentences.zh: 他后来成为了美国医学会主席。

sentences.en: It is true, though, that some of the things that Marion Sims discovered
sentences.zh: 他是纽约医学科学院的成员。

sentences.en: are still being used or in form medical practice today.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个非常矛盾的遗产，因为他帮助开创或发明的某些东西，

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 可能确实对我们今天有用，我们重视并受益于这些知识。

sentences.en: He went on to become president of the American Medical Association.
sentences.zh: 然而，这些知识是以如此巨大的代价获得的。

sentences.en: He was a member of the New York Academy of Medicine.
sentences.zh: 它是以巨大的代价获得的。

sentences.en: So this is a very conflicted legacy because presumably some of the things that he helped start
sentences.zh: 我最近读了一项由医生在2011年进行的研究。

sentences.en: or he helped invent are things that are of use to us today and we value and we benefit from that knowledge.
sentences.zh: 他们查阅了医学教科书，看看西姆斯是如何被提及的。

sentences.en: And yet that knowledge was obtained at such great coSt.
sentences.zh: 他被称为现代妇科之父，完善了外科技术的人。

sentences.en: It was obtained at great coSt.
sentences.zh: 但对于他在被奴役女性身上进行实验性手术的遗产，却只字未提。

sentences.en: And I recently read a 2011 study that was done by physicians.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: And they looked at medical textbooks to see how Sims was referred.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说，他所做的某些手术，今天的女性正在从中受益，特别是在贫穷国家。}

sentences.en: He was referred as a father of modern gynecology, someone who perfected the surgical technique.
sentences.zh: 他被称为现代妇科之父，完善了外科技术的人。

sentences.en: But no discussion about his legacy in terms of conducting these experimental surgeries on enslaved women.
sentences.zh: 但对于他在被奴役女性身上进行实验性手术的遗产，却只字未提。

sentences.en: So that's part of the problem.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是问题的一部分。

sentences.en: We can say that some of these surgeries that he did, women today are benefiting from, especially in poor countries.
sentences.zh: 我们可以说，他所做的某些手术，今天的女性正在从中受益，特别是在贫穷国家。

sentences.en: But at the same time, we can't forget how that came to be.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，我们不能忘记这一切是如何发生的。

sentences.en: I'm wondering, as someone who is a physician herself, what do you think should be done with those statues?
sentences.zh: 作为一名医生，我想请教您，您认为应该如何处理那些雕像？

sentences.en: You know, it's one of those things where I'm conflicted.
sentences.zh: 你知道，这让我感到很矛盾。

sentences.en: If you had asked me this question last spring, I would have given you a different answer.
sentences.zh: 如果你去年春天问我这个问题，我会给你一个不同的答案。

sentences.en: And I'll tell you why I'm conflicted.
sentences.zh: 我来告诉你我为什么感到矛盾。

sentences.en: Last summer, I went to Liverpool.
sentences.zh: 去年夏天，我去了利物浦。

sentences.en: And Liverpool has a remarkable international museum of slavery.
sentences.zh: 利物浦有一个非常出色的国际奴隶制博物馆。

sentences.en: And one of the things that I did when I was in Liverpool, I took a slavery history tour.
sentences.zh: 在利物浦时，我参加了一次奴隶制历史之旅。

sentences.en: And on an art deco building, there was an image of Neptune, since it's Liverpool and water.
sentences.zh: 在一栋装饰艺术风格的建筑上，有一幅海神的画像，因为利物浦与水息息相关。

sentences.en: And underneath Neptune, there were two black children who were in chains.
sentences.zh: 在海神下方，有两个被锁链锁住的黑人孩子。

sentences.en: And the tour guide, who was an 80-plus-year-old black gentleman, asked us,
sentences.zh: 导游是一位80多岁的黑人老先生，他问我们：

sentences.en: do you think this should be taken down?
sentences.zh: 你们认为这应该被拆除吗？

sentences.en: And most people said yes.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都说应该。

sentences.en: And he says, I think it should stay.
sentences.zh: 他说，我认为它应该保留。

sentences.en: And he said, I think it should stay, because I don't want people to forget it happened.
sentences.zh: 他说，我认为它应该保留，因为我不希望人们忘记这段历史。

sentences.en: And so I think that we need to do something to commemorate the women, to add something to say,
sentences.zh: 所以我认为我们需要做点什么来纪念这些女性，补充一些内容来说明：

sentences.en: yes, Sims did this, but what about Annika?
sentences.zh: 是的，西姆斯确实做了这些事，但安妮卡呢？

sentences.en: What about Lucy?
sentences.zh: 露西呢？

sentences.en: What about Betsy?
sentences.zh: 贝琪呢？

sentences.en: I think if we don't do that, that people will forget what happened to those women.
sentences.zh: 我想如果我们不这样做，人们就会忘记这些女性身上发生过什么。

sentences.en: So, as a historian and as a teacher, I think that it's important for people to know what happened to those women.
sentences.zh: 因此，作为一名历史学家和教师，我认为让人们了解这些女性的遭遇非常重要。

sentences.en: And if we whisk away these images of Sims, people will forget.
sentences.zh: 如果我们抹去这些关于西姆斯的影像，人们就会遗忘。

sentences.en: How do you hear what these women were going through?
sentences.zh: 你如何去倾听这些女性曾经经历过什么？

sentences.en: So if you could speak to Annika and Lucy and Betsy, what do you think they would tell you?
sentences.zh: 如果能与安妮卡、露西和贝琪对话，你认为她们会告诉你什么？

sentences.en: I think the story they would tell me would not start with SiMs.
sentences.zh: 我认为她们告诉我的故事不会从西姆斯开始。

sentences.en: I think the story they would tell me would be about their lives as enslaved women.
sentences.zh: 我认为她们会讲述作为被奴役女性的生活。

sentences.en: It would begin there.
sentences.zh: 故事会从那里开始。

sentences.en: It would begin how there were times where if that baby had survived, that the baby would have been taken away from them.
sentences.zh: 会从那些时刻开始：如果孩子活下来，孩子也会被从她们身边夺走。

sentences.en: They would talk to me about how, as being black women, their bodies were used sexually, that they did not have consent,
sentences.zh: 她们会告诉我，作为黑人女性，她们的身体如何被性剥削，她们没有选择权，

sentences.en: and that what happened to them with Sims was part and parcel of what their lives were at that particular time.
sentences.zh: 以及她们在西姆斯身上经历的一切，正是她们那个时代生活的一部分。

sentences.en: But I think the other thing they would want us to know is that they were human beings and that they also deserve their story to be memorialized.
sentences.zh: 但我认为她们还希望我们知道，她们是活生生的人，她们的故事也值得被铭记。

sentences.en: If you could build a memorial to Annika, Betsy and Lucy, or a memorial that stood alongside the memorials that we have erected to Marion Sims in South Carolina and New York City,
sentences.zh: 如果你能为安妮卡、贝琪和露西建立一座纪念碑，或者一座与我们在南卡罗来纳州和纽约市为马里昂·西姆斯竖立的纪念碑并排的纪念碑，

sentences.en: what would the memorial say?
sentences.zh: 这座纪念碑上会写什么？

sentences.en: The statue would not be of the experiments, because I think that it's important not just to think of them as victims of these experiments.
sentences.zh: 雕像不会表现那些实验，因为我认为不仅要把她们视为这些实验的受害者，这一点很重要。

sentences.en: It might be with the three of them together, or it might be with their holding children, that they were mothers, that they were women.
sentences.zh: 它可能是她们三个人在一起，或者她们抱着孩子，表现她们是母亲，是女性。

sentences.en: So that's what would be part of it.
sentences.zh: 这就是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So it would not be their prostrate on the altar of science.
sentences.zh: 所以它不会是她们匍匐在科学祭坛上的样子。

sentences.en: I think what the inscription would say is,
sentences.zh: 我想碑文会写：

sentences.en: Betsy, Annika, and Lucy, the mothers of modern gynecomology.
sentences.zh: 贝琪、安妮卡和露西，现代妇科医学之母。

sentences.en: It is a checkliSt.
sentences.zh: 这是一个检查清单。

sentences.en: Can you imagine anything worse than this?
sentences.zh: 你能想象比这更糟糕的事情吗？

sentences.en: If the answer is no, ask again.
sentences.zh: 如果答案是否定的，那就再问一遍。

sentences.en: Bettina Judd is a professor of gender and women's studies at the College of William and Mary.
sentences.zh: 贝蒂娜·贾德是威廉与玛丽学院性别与女性研究专业的教授。

sentences.en: She's also a poet.
sentences.zh: 她也是一位诗人。

sentences.en: And she recently wrote about a medical experience she had in a book called Patient,
sentences.zh: 她最近在一本名为《病人》的书里写到了她的一次医疗经历，

sentences.en: drawing not just on her personal history as a black woman,
sentences.zh: 不仅借鉴了她作为黑人女性的个人历史，

sentences.en: but the stories of Annika, Betsy, and Lucy.
sentences.zh: 还借鉴了安妮卡、贝琪和露西的故事。

sentences.en: Producer Maggie Penman spoke to Bettina Judd and asked her to read some of her poetry.
sentences.zh: 制作人玛吉·彭曼采访了贝蒂娜·贾德，并请她朗读了一些诗作。

sentences.en: In 2006, in her first year of graduate school, Bettina Judd had what she calls an ordeal with medicine.
sentences.zh: 2006年，在研究生一年级时，贝蒂娜·贾德经历了一场她所说的“医疗磨难”。

sentences.en: She was driving home from her part-time job and had to pull over because of a sharp pain in her abdomen.
sentences.zh: 她下班开车回家时，因为腹部剧痛不得不靠边停车。

sentences.en: In 2006, I had an ordeal with medicine.
sentences.zh: 2006年，我经历了一场医疗磨难。

sentences.en: I must have been found guilty of something.
sentences.zh: 我一定是被判有罪了。

sentences.en: I don't feel innocent here, lurking with ghosts.
sentences.zh: 我在这里感觉不到清白，与幽灵潜伏在一起。

sentences.en: See, it happens like that.
sentences.zh: 看，事情就是这样发生的。

sentences.en: I start at a thought that is quite benign and end up peckined, debased.
sentences.zh: 我从一个非常温和的想法开始，最终却变得卑微、堕落。

sentences.en: I had an ordeal with medicine and was found innocent or guilty.
sentences.zh: 我经历了一场医疗磨难，被判定无罪或有罪。

sentences.en: It feels the same because I live in a haunted house.
sentences.zh: 感觉都一样，因为我住在一座闹鬼的房子里。

sentences.en: A house can be a dynasty, a bloodline, a body.
sentences.zh: 房子可以是王朝、血统、身体。

sentences.en: There was punishment, like the way the body is murdered by its own weight when lynched.
sentences.zh: 有惩罚，就像身体在被私刑处死时被自身的重量谋杀一样。

sentences.en: Not that I was wrong, but that verdicts come in a bloodline.
sentences.zh: 不是我错了，而是判决来自血统。

sentences.en: In 2006, I had an ordeal with medicine.
sentences.zh: 2006年，我经历了一场医疗磨难。

sentences.en: To recover, I learn why ghosts come to me.
sentences.zh: 为了康复，我了解了为什么幽灵会来找我。

sentences.en: The research question is, why am I patient?
sentences.zh: 研究问题是，为什么我是病人？

sentences.en: Bettina Judd had to be patient, as a doctor told her she was having menstrual cramps and sent her home with painkillers.
sentences.zh: 贝蒂娜·贾德不得不保持耐心，因为医生告诉她只是痛经，并让她带着止痛药回家。

sentences.en: A few days later, she was told she had a bladder infection and given antibiotics.
sentences.zh: 几天后，她被告知患有膀胱感染，并服用了抗生素。

sentences.en: She was repeatedly given pregnancy tests, though she had told doctors she wasn't having sex with men.
sentences.zh: 她被反复要求做妊娠测试，尽管她告诉医生她没有与男性发生性关系。

sentences.en: She didn't know it at the time, but what she was suffering from was an ovarian torsion,
sentences.zh: 当时她并不知道，她患的是卵巢扭转，

sentences.en: a rotation of the ovary that makes it impossible for blood to flow to it.
sentences.zh: 卵巢旋转导致血液无法流入。

sentences.en: She was experiencing the death of one of her organs.
sentences.zh: 她正在经历器官坏死。

sentences.en: There might be something called an inpatient.
sentences.zh: 也许有一种东西叫住院病人。

sentences.en: Pregnancy tests, doctor's whispers, my week-long funk, sterile lubricant, discarded speculuMs.
sentences.zh: 妊娠测试、医生的耳语、我长达一周的沮丧、无菌润滑剂、废弃的窥器。

sentences.en: Every wear of morphine mimics a familiar morning.
sentences.zh: 每一次吗啡的药效都模仿着一个熟悉的早晨。

sentences.en: Another dream of drowning in mucus, meeting a dead ovary.
sentences.zh: 又一个溺死在粘液中的梦，遇见一个坏死的卵巢。

sentences.en: She floats in yellow, spits ovum into the poison, wrinkles black in mourning.
sentences.zh: 她在黄色中漂浮，将卵子吐进毒药中，黑色的皱纹在哀悼。

sentences.en: Throughout this ordeal, Bettina kept thinking about an article she had read not long before she became ill,
sentences.zh: 在整个磨难过程中，贝蒂娜一直在思考她在生病前不久读过的一篇文章，

sentences.en: about J.
sentences.zh: 关于J.

sentences.en: Marion Sims, who operated on slave women in the 1840s.
sentences.zh: 马里昂·西姆斯，他在19世纪40年代对奴隶女性进行了手术。

sentences.en: Anarcha, Betsy, and Lucy began to haunt her morphine-fueled dreaMs.
sentences.zh: 安娜卡、贝琪和露西开始在她吗啡引发的梦境中萦绕。

sentences.en: She tried to understand what was happening to her through their stories.
sentences.zh: 她试图通过她们的故事来理解自己身上发生的事情。

sentences.en: Nurses ask me, how much does it hurt on a scale from 1 to 10?
sentences.zh: 护士问我，疼痛程度从1到10是多少？

sentences.en: Anarcha Westcott, Betsy Harris, and Lucy Zimmerman
sentences.zh: 安娜卡·韦斯科特、贝琪·哈里斯和露西·齐默尔曼

sentences.en: are taken into the care of a reluctant country surgeon in Montgomery, Alabama.
sentences.zh: 被交由阿拉巴马州蒙哥马利市一位不情愿的乡村外科医生照料。

sentences.en: See blood on a white hospital sheet?
sentences.zh: 看到白色病床单上的血迹了吗？

sentences.en: Tell me I'm having menstrual cramps, Betsy's first birth.
sentences.zh: 告诉我我只是痛经，贝琪的第一次分娩。

sentences.en: Send me home with oxycodone, ibuprofen, Lucy months out of household duties.
sentences.zh: 让我带着羟考酮、布洛芬回家，露西几个月没做家务。

sentences.en: After five hours in triage, Anarcha, his first vesicovaginal fistula,
sentences.zh: 在分诊台待了五个小时后，安娜卡，他第一个膀胱阴道瘘病例，

sentences.en: and another prescription, in these three, Sims shapes his speculum, invents his silver sutures,
sentences.zh: 还有另一张处方，在这三个人身上，西姆斯塑造了他的窥器，发明了他的银缝线，

sentences.en: perfects protocol for proper handling of the female pelvis.
sentences.zh: 完善了处理女性骨盆的规程。

sentences.en: We wake, unanesthetized or addicted to opium.
sentences.zh: 我们醒来，没有麻醉或沉迷于鸦片。

sentences.en: Children born, children disappeared.
sentences.zh: 孩子出生，孩子消失。

sentences.en: Helpless.
sentences.zh: 无助。

sentences.en: Help.
sentences.zh: 救命。

sentences.en: She kept being asked this question,
sentences.zh: 她一直被问到这个问题，

sentences.en: what is your pain on a scale from 1 to 10?
sentences.zh: 你的疼痛程度从1到10是多少？

sentences.en: And she would ask herself, well, what is 1?
sentences.zh: 她会问自己，嗯，1是什么？

sentences.en: What is 10?
sentences.zh: 10是什么？

sentences.en: If I say it's a 10, what will they think?
sentences.zh: 如果我说10，他们会怎么想？

sentences.en: They'll see me, a young African-American woman, alone.
sentences.zh: 他们会看到我，一个年轻的非裔美国女性，孤身一人。

sentences.en: Will they think I'm looking for pain pills?
sentences.zh: 他们会认为我在找止痛药吗？

sentences.en: I'll give it a 7.
sentences.zh: 我给7分吧。

sentences.en: Betsy invents the speculum.
sentences.zh: 贝琪发明了窥器。

sentences.en: Fall, 1845.
Introducing the bent handle of the spoon,
sentences.zh: 引入弯曲的勺柄，

sentences.en: I saw everything as no man had ever seen before,
sentences.zh: 我看到了前人从未见过的景象，

sentences.en: from the story of my life, by J.
sentences.zh: 摘自《我的一生》，作者J.

sentences.en: Marion SiMs.
sentences.zh: 马里昂·西姆斯。

sentences.en: I have bent in other ways,
sentences.zh: 我以其他方式弯曲，

sentences.en: to open the body, make space.
sentences.zh: 打开身体，创造空间。

sentences.en: More pliable than pewter,
sentences.zh: 比白镴更柔韧，

sentences.en: my skin may be less giving.
sentences.zh: 我的皮肤可能没那么容易屈服。

sentences.en: Great discoveries are made on cushioned lessons
sentences.zh: 伟大的发现建立在缓冲的教训

sentences.en: and hard falls.
sentences.zh: 和沉重的跌倒之上。

sentences.en: Sims invents the speculum.
sentences.zh: 西姆斯发明了窥器。

sentences.en: I invent the wincing,
sentences.zh: 我发明了畏缩，

sentences.en: the if-you-must of it,
sentences.zh: 那种“如果必须”的无奈，

sentences.en: the looking away,
sentences.zh: 那种移开视线，

sentences.en: the here of discovery.
sentences.zh: 那种发现的当下。

sentences.en: Finally, Bettina ended up in a third hospital,
sentences.zh: 最后，贝蒂娜住进了第三家医院，

sentences.en: this time a teaching hospital
sentences.zh: 这次是一家教学医院，

sentences.en: in an African-American neighborhood in her hometown.
sentences.zh: 位于她家乡的一个非裔美国人社区。

sentences.en: One day, after multiple pelvic exams,
sentences.zh: 有一天，在多次盆腔检查后，

sentences.en: after questions about her sexual history,
sentences.zh: 在被问及性史后，

sentences.en: after her answers not being believed,
sentences.zh: 在她的回答不被相信后，

sentences.en: she had a moment of outburSt.
sentences.zh: 她爆发了。

sentences.en: She sat aloud in a room full of doctors.
sentences.zh: 她在满屋子的医生面前大声说出来。

sentences.en: Gynecology was built on the backs of black women anyway.
sentences.zh: 反正妇科医学是建立在黑人女性的背上的。

sentences.en: To the patient.
sentences.zh: 致病人。

sentences.en: Tears will only leave you wanting for water
sentences.zh: 眼泪只会让你渴望水

sentences.en: and more time.
sentences.zh: 和更多的时间。

sentences.en: Which, as you know,
sentences.zh: 正如你所知，

sentences.en: will be spent waiting.
sentences.zh: 这些时间都将花在等待上。

sentences.en: It's been ten years since Bettina Judd
sentences.zh: 距离贝蒂娜·贾德

sentences.en: had her ordeal with medicine.
sentences.zh: 经历那场医疗磨难已经十年了。

sentences.en: Next week, she'll be in Columbia, South Carolina,
sentences.zh: 下周，她将前往南卡罗来纳州的哥伦比亚市，

sentences.en: and she's going to see the statue of Sims,
sentences.zh: 她要去看看西姆斯的雕像，

sentences.en: which she says she hopes will stay up for now.
sentences.zh: 她说她希望雕像暂时保留。

sentences.en: Until we have a conversation about who Sims was,
sentences.zh: 直到我们开始讨论西姆斯是谁，

sentences.en: and who the women he operated on were.
sentences.zh: 以及他手术的那些女性是谁。

sentences.en: Until there's a statue of Anarka,
sentences.zh: 直到有一座安娜卡、

sentences.en: Lucy, and Betsy,
sentences.zh: 露西和贝琪的雕像，

sentences.en: the mothers of gynecology.
sentences.zh: 妇科医学之母。

sentences.en: A statue, she says,
sentences.zh: 她说，一座雕像，

sentences.en: that she hopes will be bigger
sentences.zh: 她希望它比

sentences.en: than the statue of SiMs.
sentences.zh: 西姆斯的雕像更大。

sentences.en: Producer Maggie Penman
sentences.zh: 制作人玛吉·彭曼

sentences.en: and Bettina Jani.
sentences.zh: 和贝蒂娜·贾德。
